what: blaze-link's patch says whether it applies to an empty file (a full patch leaves zero runs unwritten) or to a clone; the driver's Patch has no such flag and is always applied to a clone of the old image. Fitting one to the other, program::patch_of writes zeros over every unwritten run below the old length when a full patch follows an earlier image.
cost: On a relink that found no room in place, up to a whole image of zeros copied into the patch and written, where an empty file would cost none.
cause: The two patch types were designed in two lanes; the driver's dropped the base the linker's carries.
whys: Why zeros? The clone holds the old image's bytes where the full patch assumes zeros.
Why no flag? The driver's doc says a first link writes over an empty file, which is the only full patch it imagined.
class: A seam type that drops a variant its producer has.
prevention: Give the driver's Patch a `base: PatchBase` (or `from_empty: bool`) and let Images::make start an empty file for it.
workaround: program::patch_of fills the gaps with zero writes.
state: resolved: the driver's Patch has `base: PatchBase`; program::patch_of sets it and the zero fill is gone (2026-11-14)
